findings.problem: `slice` re-proves, line for line, what `isIntegrallyClosed_ImK` and `tmul_mem_ImK` prove later. The shared part is the DVR instance, the IsScalarTower instance, the 15-line CharP argument for the residue field, the CharZero/hGFN/hNBI extraction, the `hφ'`/`hφ` flatness injectivity argument, and the `IsIntegrallyClosed.of_equiv (AlgEquiv.ofInjective …)` step. `slice` takes `φ.range` as its subalgebra, while the later declarations name the same thing `ImK := (φK …).range`. The final membership proof in `slice` (`refine ⟨… ⊗ₜ b, ?_⟩; change φ … ; rw [Algebra.TensorProduct.map_tmul]; rfl`) is the same as the body of `tmul_mem_ImK`. `slice` is not used by `isIntegrallyClosed_tensor` or `chart`, which use `ImK`. Keeping both copies means any change to the CharP or flatness argument must be made twice.
findings.proposed_change:
Move `slice` after the `SliceDefs` section, or delete it if nothing outside needs it. Replace its body by the existing declarations:
`theorem slice … := ⟨ImK Γ ℓ A hρ S K, isIntegrallyClosed_ImK Γ ℓ A hρ S K hA hNBI hGFN, fun x hx b => tmul_mem_ImK Γ ℓ A hρ S K x hx b⟩`.
The statement and hypotheses are unchanged. `isIntegrallyClosed_ImK` and `tmul_mem_ImK` are both declared with `omit hcT`, so their argument lists match what `slice` can supply. `slice` itself still takes `hcT` through `include`, which is harmless. This removes about 60 lines, including the whole CharP block.
findings.benefit: One copy of the CharP, DVR and flatness reasoning remains. A reader no longer has to check that two long proofs say the same thing. A future fix to the residue-characteristic argument cannot be applied to one theorem and forgotten in the other.

have hφ' : ∀ t, φ t = ((inclK ℓ A hρ K).toLinearMap.rTensor S) t := by
    intro t
    induction t using TensorProduct.induction_on with
    | zero => simp
    | tmul a b => rw [Algebra.TensorProduct.map_tmul, LinearMap.rTensor_tmul]; rfl
    | add x y hx hy => rw [map_add, map_add, hx, hy]
  have hφ : Function.Injective φ := by
    intro x y h
    rw [hφ', hφ'] at h
    exact Module.Flat.rTensor_preserves_injective_linearMap _ (inclK_injective ℓ A hρ K) h
findings.problem: The same argument appears three times. The map `Algebra.TensorProduct.map f (AlgHom.id R S)` agrees with `f.toLinearMap.rTensor S`, shown by `TensorProduct.induction_on`. It is therefore injective when `f` is injective and `S` is flat. The copies are `hφ'`/`hφ` in `slice` (lines 496-505), `hφ'`/`hφ` in `isIntegrallyClosed_ImK` (lines 615-624), and `hΦ'`/`hΦ` in `sliceNormal` (lines 752-761). `slice` and `isIntegrallyClosed_ImK` also end with the same step: injective alg hom to a range-isomorphism to `IsIntegrallyClosed.of_equiv`. Each copy is a 4-case induction followed by a rewrite, which is real proof content, not a one-line unfold. I found no Mathlib lemma stating this fact.
findings.proposed_change:
Add a lemma in `FibreIsoAux`, or near the top of `IgusaICH`:
`theorem map_id_injective {R A B S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing S] [Algebra R A] [Algebra R B] [Algebra R S] [Module.Flat R S] (f : A →ₐ[R] B) (hf : Function.Injective f) : Function.Injective (Algebra.TensorProduct.map f (AlgHom.id R S))`.
Proof sketch: show `Algebra.TensorProduct.map f (AlgHom.id R S) t = (f.toLinearMap.rTensor S) t` by `TensorProduct.induction_on`, using `Algebra.TensorProduct.map_tmul` and `LinearMap.rTensor_tmul`. Then conclude with `Module.Flat.rTensor_preserves_injective_linearMap _ hf`.
Uses: in `isIntegrallyClosed_ImK`, `hφ := map_id_injective (inclK ℓ A hρ K) (inclK_injective ℓ A hρ K)`, using `φK` unfolded by `rfl`. In `sliceNormal`, `hΦ := map_id_injective resK hres_inj`. `slice` disappears per finding 1. Each use needs only `[Module.Flat ℤℓ S]`, which both theorems already have in scope as `flat_S Γ ℓ S`.
Optionally add `IsIntegrallyClosed.of_equiv_ofInjective`, whose statement is `Function.Injective φ → IsIntegrallyClosed ↥φ.range ← IsIntegrallyClosed source`, to cover the `AlgEquiv.ofInjective` plus `of_equiv` step that also occurs in `chart`.
findings.benefit: The three 10-line induction blocks become one-line calls. The mathematical point, that flatness plus injectivity gives injective base change, gets a name. A reader of `sliceNormal` and `isIntegrallyClosed_ImK` sees the intent directly instead of re-reading an induction.
